name: Zanubrutinib (continuous, CLL/SLL)
disease: Chronic lymphocytic leukemia / small lymphocytic lymphoma (CLL/SLL)
histology: chronic lymphocytic leukemia / small lymphocytic lymphoma

biomarkers.TP53: test at each line of therapy
biomarkers.del17p: test at each line of therapy
biomarkers.note: Test for del(17p) and TP53 mutation (and IGHV mutation status) before each line of therapy. Zanubrutinib, a next-generation covalent BTK inhibitor, is preferred and effective REGARDLESS of del(17p)/TP53 status and is a preferred option specifically for del(17p)/TP53-aberrant CLL, where chemoimmunotherapy is inferior and should be avoided. Per Standard Guidelines (NCCN), CLL/SLL, v2.2026, CSLL-4.
biomarkers.efficacyNote: Zanubrutinib demonstrated improved efficacy and a favorable safety profile versus bendamustine/rituximab (SEQUOIA) and versus ibrutinib (ALPINE).

treatmentSetting: first-line and relapsed/refractory therapy for CLL/SLL requiring treatment
lineOfTherapy: first-line (Preferred, category 1) and second-line or subsequent therapy (Preferred, category 1) for CLL/SLL, with or without del(17p)/TP53 mutation

eligibilityCriteria.requirement: CLL/SLL meeting iwCLL indications for treatment (not asymptomatic early-stage disease)
eligibilityCriteria.locator: v2.2026, CSLL-3 (indications for treatment) and CSLL-4 (First-Line Therapy)

eligibilityCriteria.requirement: del(17p)/TP53 testing performed; zanubrutinib is preferred for del(17p)/TP53-aberrant disease (avoid chemoimmunotherapy)
eligibilityCriteria.locator: v2.2026, CSLL-4 (CLL/SLL with del(17p)/TP53 Mutation: Zanubrutinib (continuous), Preferred)

drugs.name: Zanubrutinib

provenance.locator: CSLL-4 (First-Line Therapy: Zanubrutinib (continuous), Preferred, category 1); MS narrative (cBTKis are given continuously until disease progression)

drugs.notes: Zanubrutinib is given continuously (days 1 to 28 represent continuous daily oral dosing; a BTK inhibitor is not cycled), until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity per Standard Guidelines (NCCN), CLL/SLL v2.2026. DOSE IS VERIFY: the provided source confirms continuous dosing but does not print the dose; the commonly cited product-label dose is 160 mg PO twice daily OR 320 mg PO once daily, which must be VERIFY-confirmed against the label before use (not asserted here).

supportiveCare: Continuous daily oral therapy; adherence is critical to maintaining disease control.
Monitor for atrial fibrillation, hypertension, bleeding, neutropenia, and infection (BTK-inhibitor class effects); zanubrutinib has a lower atrial-fibrillation signal than ibrutinib.
Consider antiviral/antimicrobial prophylaxis per institutional practice.

monitoring: CBC with differential and platelets periodically
blood pressure and cardiac rhythm (atrial fibrillation) surveillance

doseModificationRules.condition: grade 3 to 4 non-hematologic toxicity or grade 4 hematologic toxicity
doseModificationRules.text: Interrupt and resume zanubrutinib at a reduced dose per prescribing information after recovery; clinical review.

core.source: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 12th ed.
core.locator: zanubrutinib is a highly selective next-generation covalent BTK inhibitor (CLL/lymphoma chapters); dose not printed in the provided extract

guideline.locator: CSLL-4 (First-Line Therapy, Preferred: Zanubrutinib (continuous), category 1; both with and without del(17p)/TP53 mutation); CSLL-D 2 of 5 (Second-Line or Subsequent: Zanubrutinib continuous, category 1); MS (cBTKis given continuously until progression; SEQUOIA, ALPINE)

provenanceNote: ONCQIS Standard Protocol draft for continuous single-agent zanubrutinib in CLL/SLL (#73). Zanubrutinib is a Preferred, category 1 option in both first-line (CSLL-4) and second-line/subsequent (CSLL-D 2 of 5) therapy per Standard Guidelines (NCCN), CLL/SLL v2.2026, and is effective and preferred with or without del(17p)/TP53 mutation, where chemoimmunotherapy should be avoided. Modeled as continuous daily oral therapy (cycleLengthDays 28 for reporting, cycles null, days 1 to 28 = continuous) because a BTK inhibitor is taken continuously, not in discrete cycles. DOSE IS VERIFY: the provided sources confirm continuous administration but do not print the dose; per the hard grounding rule the dose is set to the literal VERIFY (the commonly cited label dose of 160 mg PO twice daily or 320 mg PO once daily is noted for clinical context only and is not asserted from a cited source). verifyFields lists the VERIFY dose and the protocol stays at DRAFT. This remains a StewardMD Standard Protocol; no endorsement implied.
